verses.sanskrit: नारद उवाच। गयं चामूर्तरयसं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम।  यो वै वर्षशतं राजा हुतशिष्टाशनोऽभवत् ॥१॥
verses.english: Narada said O Srinjaya, we also heard of the death of king Gaya, the son of Amurtarajas, who for hundred years lived only upon remnants of the libations offered on fire.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मै ह्यग्निर्वरं प्रादात् ततो वव्रे वरं गयः। तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण व्रतेन नियमेन च ॥२॥
गुरूणां च प्रसादेन वेदानिच्छामि वेदितुम्।  स्वधर्मेणाविहिंस्यान्यान् धनमिच्छामि चाक्षयम् ॥३॥
verses.english: Thereat Agni offered to bestow boon on him; and thereupon Gaya asked for this boon saying, "I desire to acquaint myself with the contents of the Vedas, through ascetic penances, observance of Brahmacharya rites, vows and rules and also through the grace of my preceptors. I also desire to acquire inexhaustible wealth without transgressing the duties of the order which I belong to and without any injury to any one else.

verses.sanskrit: विप्रेषु ददतश्चैव श्रद्धा भवतु नित्यशः।  अनन्यासु सवर्णासु पुत्रजन्म च मे भवेत् ॥४॥
verses.english: I desire also the boon, that everyday I may give away devoutly my wealth to the Brahmanas. I wish also to beget sons upon females of my own order and not upon others.

verses.sanskrit: अन्नं मे ददतः श्रद्धा धर्मे मे रमतां मनः।  अविघ्नं चास्तु मे नित्यं धर्मकार्येषु पावक ॥५॥
verses.english: Let devotion be the ruling feeling of my heart when I shall give away edibles; let also my mind delight in the fountain of righteousness. Let, O Agni, no difficulty overtake me when I engage myself in the performance of pious deeds."

verses.sanskrit: तथा भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत।  गयो ह्यवाप्य तत्सर्वं धर्मेणारीनजीजयत् ॥६॥
verses.english: "It shall be so", saying this, the God of Fire, disappeared even there. Then Gaya realising all those boons sought, began to obtain righteous victories over all his enemies.

verses.sanskrit: स दर्शपौर्णमासीभ्यां कालेष्वाग्रयणेन च।  चातुर्मास्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैश्चावाप्तदक्षिणैः ॥७॥
verses.english: Then king Gaya celebrated for a full hundred years, various kinds of sacrifices with profuse Dakshinas, as also many other vows as Chaturmasya.

verses.sanskrit: अयजच्छ्रद्धया राजा परिसंवत्सरान् शतम्।  गवां शतसहस्राणि शतमश्वशतानि च ॥८॥
verses.english: Every year, in a century, the king gave unto the Brahmanas, with due devotion, hundred thousand kine, ten thousand horses.

verses.sanskrit: शतं निष्कसहस्राणि गवां चाप्ययुतानि षट्।  उत्थायोत्थाय स प्रादात् परिसंवत्सरान् शतम् ॥९॥
verses.english: And for several successive centuries he gave to the Brahmanas hundred thousand Nishkas and sixty-thousand kine, at the time of his rising.

verses.sanskrit: नक्षत्रेषु च सर्वेषु ददन्नक्षत्रदक्षिणाः।  ईजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्यथा सोमोऽङ्गिरा यथा ॥१०॥
सौवर्णां पृथिवीं कृत्वा य इमां मणिशर्कराम्। विप्रेभ्यः प्राददद्राजा सोऽश्वमेधे महामखे ॥११॥
verses.english: Making the earth covered with gold and with pebbles constituted by gems, he gave her away as a present to the Brahmanas during the celebration of his great Horse-sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: जाम्बूनदमया यूपाः सर्वे रत्नपरिच्छदाः।  गयस्यासन् समृद्धास्तु सर्वभूतमनोहराः ॥१२॥
verses.english: In the sacrifices of Gaya, the stakes were made of gold; and embossed with jewels and precious, they delighted the hearts of all.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वकामसमृद्धं च प्रादादन्नं गयस्तदा।  ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रहृष्टेभ्यः सर्वभूतेभ्य एव च ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then Gaya gave to the delighted Brahmanas and other creatures, those stakes and many other precious objects of desire.

verses.sanskrit: स समुद्रवनद्वीपनदीनदवनेषु च। नगरेषु च राष्ट्रेषु दिवि व्योम्नि च येऽवसन् ॥१४॥
verses.english: The various species of creatures inhabiting the oceans, the islands, the rivers male and female, the woods, forests, towns, kingdoms, the paradise and the sky and diverse other beings were gratified with the wealth and riches distributed at Gaya's sacrifice. They then said, "There was no sacrifice like that celebrated by Gaya."

verses.sanskrit: भूतग्रामाश्च विविधाः सन्तृप्ता यज्ञसम्पदा।  गयस्य सदृशो यज्ञो नास्त्यन्य इति तेऽब्रुवन् ॥१५॥
षट्त्रिंशद्योजनायामा त्रिंशद्योजनमायता।  पश्चात् पुरश्चतुर्विंशद्वेदी ह्यासीद्धिरण्मयी ॥१६॥
verses.english: The sacrificial altar of Gaya was thirty yojanas long, twenty-six yojanas high; and it was covered with gold and strewn over with pearls and gems. He gave away this altar and inany garments and ornaments to the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: गयस्य यजमानस्य मुक्ता वज्रमणिस्तृता।  प्रादात् स ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽथ वासांस्याभरणानि च ॥१७॥
यथोक्ता दक्षिणाश्चान्या विप्रेभ्यो भूरिदक्षिणः। यत्र भोजनशिष्टस्य पर्वताः पञ्चविंशतिः॥१८॥
कुल्याः कुशलवाहिन्यो रसानामभवंस्तदा।  वस्त्राभरणगन्धानां राशयश्च पृथग्विधाः ॥१९॥
verses.english: And there also remained many lakes of potions and several stream of juicy drinks flowing charmingly and many garments and rnaments, perfumes and many princes (who were intended to be given away as presents).

verses.sanskrit: यस्य प्रभावाच्च गयस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः।  वटश्चाक्षय्यकरणः पुण्यं ब्रह्मसरश्च तत् ॥२०॥
स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः।  अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभिश्वैत्येति व्याहरन् ॥२१॥
